newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SAMURAIS BOOST A$ AT MARGIN - RBA'S FRASER.
newsitem.headline: SAMURAIS BOOST A$ AT MARGIN - RBA'S FRASER.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Bernie Fraser said recent strong samurai bond issuance contributed at the margin to keeping the Australian dollar up.

"The inflow is contributing at the margin at the moment to holding the exchange rate up, but that's not a matter for concern," Fraser said after a BZW seminar in Tokyo. His comments were relayed by Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
Fraser said the increased Samurai issuance was a reflection of improved confidence in the changes made to the Australian economy in recent years, the lower inflation rate and a stable currency.
A samurai is a bond issued in Japan by a non-Japanese borrower and denominated in yen.

Dual-currency samurais are issued in yen, and interest is paid in yen, but they are redeemed in other currencies, mainly in the Australian dollar, followed by the U.S. dollar and the New Zealand dollar.

Japan Ministry of Finance statistics show that the total volume of samurais issued from January to June amounted to 1.799 trillion yen ($16.5 billion). Of that, 1.089 trillion yen ($9.9 billion) was dual-currency issues.
MOF officials have said that even at peak times in the past, the annual volume had been no higher than around 650 billion yen ($5.96 billion).
The bonds are not subject to Japanese withholding taxes, and therefore offer advantages to Japanese buyers.
